interest: Japan's jury law, 1944 home-front measures and planning for Japan's territories.
overview: This file comprises records from the Department of State's Central Decimal Files (file classification 894.044, relating to the judicial branch, laws, statutes, and decrees of Japan) spanning from July 1940 to March 1944. The collection opens with a July 1940 Military Attaché report from Tokyo detailing the statutory framework, jurisdiction, qualifications, and exemptions of the Japanese jury trial system established under the Jury Law of 1923. It is followed by two March 1944 telegrams from U.S. Ambassador W. Averell Harriman in Moscow transmitting translated Japanese press reports regarding sweeping emergency wartime decrees—including total student mobilization, female labor service, civil air defense dispersals, office streamlining, and the closure of entertainment establishments. The file concludes with a June 1943 State Department memorandum of conversation between Isaiah Bowman and George H. Blakeslee outlining the schedule and agenda of the Territorial Subcommittee concerning surrender terms, administration of Korea, and the postwar detachment of Japan's outlying island territories.

subfiles.about: A digest of the 1923 Japanese law instituting trial by jury in criminal cases, outlining jurisdiction, juror qualifications, and statutory exclusions.
subfiles.summary: Military Attaché report on Japan's 1923 Jury Law, its exceptions and juror qualifications.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report on the Jury System in Japan

subfiles.about: Telegraphic report from Moscow transmitting Japanese announcements of four emergency wartime decrees regarding austerity and administrative streamlining.
subfiles.summary: Harriman reports Japan's February 29, 1944 emergency measures: closing luxury venues, cutting holidays, limiting travel and destroying records.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Harriman (Moscow) on Japanese Extraordinary Wartime Measures

subfiles.about: Telegraphic report from Moscow detailing further Japanese wartime emergency decrees involving student mobilization, women's labor, and air raid precautions.
subfiles.summary: Harriman reports Japan's emergency decrees mobilizing students and women for labor, dispersing cities and boosting shipbuilding.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Harriman (Moscow) on Mobilization and Air Defense Decrees in Japan

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum of conversation outlining the schedule and agenda of the Territorial Subcommittee on post-war Japan and East Asia.
subfiles.summary: Bowman and Blakeslee plan the 1943 Territorial Subcommittee agenda, starting with Japan's outlying islands and a plan for Korea.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on the Agenda of the Territorial Subcommittee
